**Burton Raphael Kennedy** (September 3, 1922 – February 15, 2001) was an American [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter") and [director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director") known mainly for directing [Westerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westerns "Westerns"). [Budd Boetticher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budd_Boetticher "Budd Boetticher") called him "the best Western writer ever."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burt_Kennedy&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Kennedy was born in 1922 in [Muskegon, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muskegon,_Michigan "Muskegon, Michigan"). His parents were dancers in [vaudeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaudeville "Vaudeville") and he joined their act, the Dancing Kennedys, when he was 4 years old.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-varobit-2) They moved to Michigan, where Kennedy attended high school. He graduated school in 1941 and enlisted in the army the following year. Kennedy was commissioned and saw [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") service in the [1st Cavalry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Cavalry_Division_(United_States) "1st Cavalry Division (United States)") during the [Liberation of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_Campaign_(1944%E2%80%931945) "Philippines Campaign (1944–1945)") as a first lieutenant.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-burt-3) He received the [Silver Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Star "Silver Star"), [Bronze Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_Star "Bronze Star"), and [Purple Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_Heart "Purple Heart") with [oak leaf cluster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_leaf_cluster "Oak leaf cluster").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-varobit-2)

### Early writing work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burt_Kennedy&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early writing work")]

Kennedy studied at the [Pasadena Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena_Playhouse "Pasadena Playhouse"), where he did some acting. "I'd walk out on stage and it felt like I'd been there my whole life," he recalled, but he found acting unsatisfactory. "I could see that you could be around this town for a long time before you could be a success as an actor, but writing, no one could stop you from writing. You're never out of work if you're a writer, you could just sit down and write."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-burt-3)

Kennedy found work writing for radio in 1948.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-varobit-2) He began to specialise in [Westerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westerns "Westerns"), in part due to the advice of [James Edward Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Edward_Grant "James Edward Grant"), who told him, "Why compete with all the big writers when there are hardly any good Western writers as such?" Some good writers have written Westerns, but there were very few genuine Western writers in this town that were really good writers. He said that the competition was easier that way, and if you write a good Western, you're apt to go further faster. And it turned out, he was right. Because I never stopped, from 1953 to 1954 up until the mid-'70s, I never stopped working at all."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-burt-3)

Kennedy used his training as a [cavalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavalry "Cavalry") officer to secure a job as a [fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing "Fencing") trainer and fencing stunt double in films.

### Batjac

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burt_Kennedy&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Batjac")]

Kennedy wrote 13 episodes for a proposed TV series about a Mexican, which [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne") read and tried to get financed as a vehicle for [Pedro Gonzalez Gonzalez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Gonzalez_Gonzalez "Pedro Gonzalez Gonzalez") through Wayne's [Batjac Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batjac_Productions "Batjac Productions").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Kennedy#cite_note-burt-3)

Although the TV program was never produced, it led Kennedy to write _[Seven Men from Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven\_Men\_from\_Now "Seven Men from Now")_ (1956) for Batjac. It was written for Wayne, but having just completed [John Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Ford "John Ford")'s _[The Searchers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Searchers "The Searchers")_, he wanted to take a break from Westerns, so it was made with [Randolph Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_Scott "Randolph Scott"); Wayne later expressed regret over having passed on the film. It was directed by [Budd Boetticher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budd_Boetticher "Budd Boetticher") and was the first of what became known as the "Ranown Cycle".

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Australian actor (1930–2015)

For other similarly named people, see [Rod Taylor (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Taylor_(disambiguation) "Rod Taylor (disambiguation)").

**Rodney Sturt Taylor** (11 January 1930– 7 January 2015) was an Australian actor. He appeared in more than 50 feature films, including _[Young Cassidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Cassidy "Young Cassidy")_ (1965), _[Nobody Runs Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobody\_Runs\_Forever "Nobody Runs Forever")_ (1968), _[The Train Robbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Train\_Robbers "The Train Robbers")_ (1973), and _[A Matter of Wife... and Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Matter\_of\_Wife...\_and\_Death "A Matter of Wife... and Death")_ (1975).

Taylor was born in [Lidcombe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lidcombe,_New_South_Wales "Lidcombe, New South Wales"), a suburb of [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), to a father who was a steel construction contractor and commercial artist and a mother who was a children's author. He began taking art classes in high school, and continued in college. He decided to become an actor after seeing [Laurence Olivier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier "Laurence Olivier") in an [Old Vic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Old_Vic "The Old Vic") touring production of _[Richard III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard\_III\_(play) "Richard III (play)")._

His first film role was in a re-enactment of [Charles Sturt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Sturt "Charles Sturt")'s voyage down the [Murrumbidgee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murrumbidgee_River "Murrumbidgee River") and [Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_River "Murray River") rivers, playing Sturt's offsider, [George Macleay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Macleay "George Macleay"). At the time, he was also appearing in a number of theatre productions for Australia's [Mercury Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Theatre_(Australia) "Mercury Theatre (Australia)"). He made his feature film debut in the Australian [Lee Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Robinson_(director) "Lee Robinson (director)") film _[King of the Coral Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_of\_the\_Coral\_Sea "King of the Coral Sea")_ (1954). He soon started acting in television films, portraying several different characters in the 1950s [anthology series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthology_series "Anthology series")_[Studio 57](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio\_57 "Studio 57")_.

He started to gain popularity after starring in _[The Time Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Time\_Machine\_(1960\_film) "The Time Machine (1960 film)")_ (1960), as H. George Wells. He later starred in the [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") film _[One Hundred and One Dalmatians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Hundred\_and\_One\_Dalmatians "One Hundred and One Dalmatians")_ (1961), voicing Pongo. In one of his most famous roles, he played Mitch Brenner in _[The Birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Birds\_(film) "The Birds (film)")_ (1963), directed by [Alfred Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Hitchcock "Alfred Hitchcock"). By the late 1990s, Taylor had moved into semiretirement. His final film role was in [Quentin Tarantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Tarantino "Quentin Tarantino")'s _[Inglourious Basterds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglourious\_Basterds "Inglourious Basterds")_ (2009), portraying [Winston Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill "Winston Churchill") in a cameo.

British film director (1927–2011)

For other people with the same name, see [Kenneth Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Russell_(disambiguation) "Kenneth Russell (disambiguation)").

| Born | Henry Kenneth Alfred Russell (1927-07-03)3 July 1927 [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton "Southampton"), [Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampshire "Hampshire"), England |

**Henry Kenneth Alfred Russell** (3 July 1927– 27 November 2011)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Russell#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Russell#cite_note-bbc-death-3) was a British film director known for his pioneering work in television and film, and for his flamboyant and controversial style. His films were mainly liberal adaptations of existing texts, or biographies, notably of composers of the [Romantic era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_music "Romantic music"). Russell began directing for the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), where he made creative adaptations of composers' lives which were unusual for the time. He also directed many [feature films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_film "Feature film") independently and for [studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_studio "Film studio").

Russell is best known for his [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award")-winning romantic drama film _[Women in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women\_in\_Love\_(film) "Women in Love (film)")_ (1969); the historical drama horror film _[The Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devils\_(film) "The Devils (film)")_ (1971); the musical fantasy film _[Tommy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy\_(1975\_film) "Tommy (1975 film)")_ (1975), featuring [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who"); and the science fiction horror film _[Altered States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altered\_States "Altered States")_ (1980). Russell also directed several films based on the lives of classical music composers, such as [Elgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgar_(film) "Elgar (film)"), [Delius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_Summer "Song of Summer"), [Tchaikovsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Music_Lovers "The Music Lovers"), [Mahler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler_(film) "Mahler (film)"), and [Liszt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisztomania_(film) "Lisztomania (film)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Russell#cite_note-Malcolm-4)

In 2006, film critic [Mark Kermode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kermode "Mark Kermode") attempted to sum up Russell's achievement, calling him "somebody who proved that British cinema didn't have to be about [kitchen-sink realism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchen_sink_realism "Kitchen sink realism")—it could be every bit as flamboyant as [Fellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Fellini "Federico Fellini"). Later in his life he turned to making low-budget experimental films such as _[The Lion's Mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion's\_Mouth "The Lion's Mouth")_ and _Revenge of the Elephant Man_, and they are as edgy and 'out there' as ever".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Russell#cite_note-5)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ken_Russell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

**Robert Thomas Powell** ([/ˈ p aʊ ə l/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_POW-əl_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born 1 June 1944) is an English actor who is known for the title roles in _[Mahler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler\_(film) "Mahler (film)")_ (1974) and _[Jesus of Nazareth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus\_of\_Nazareth\_(TV\_series) "Jesus of Nazareth (TV series)")_ (1977), and for his portrayal of secret agent [Richard Hannay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Hannay "Richard Hannay") in _[The Thirty Nine Steps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Thirty\_Nine\_Steps\_(1978\_film) "The Thirty Nine Steps (1978 film)")_ (1978) and its subsequent [spinoff television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannay_(TV_series) "Hannay (TV series)"). Other major screen roles have included Tobias "Toby" Wren in the BBC science-fiction programme _[Doomwatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doomwatch "Doomwatch")_ (1970), David Briggs in the sitcom _[The Detectives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Detectives\_(1993\_TV\_series) "The Detectives (1993 TV series)")_ (1993–1997) with [Jasper Carrott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasper_Carrott "Jasper Carrott"), and [Mark Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Williams_(Holby_City) "Mark Williams (Holby City)") in the medical drama _[Holby City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holby\_City "Holby City")_ (2005–2011).

Powell, with his distinctive voice, has become well known as a narrator of documentaries, especially those concerning the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), including _World War II in HD Colour_, _[Hitler's Bodyguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitler's\_Bodyguard\_(TV\_series) "Hitler's Bodyguard (TV series)")_, _The Story of the Third Reich_ and _Secrets of World War II_.

Powell was nominated for a Best Actor [BAFTA TV Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_TV_Award "BAFTA TV Award") for _Jesus of Nazareth_ in 1978 and won a Best Actor award at the [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival") for his performance in the film _[Imperative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperative\_(film) "Imperative (film)")_ in 1982.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Powell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Powell was born in [Salford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Borough_of_Salford "County Borough of Salford"), [Lancashire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancashire "Lancashire"), the son of Kathleen (née Davis) and John Wilson Powell.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Powell#cite_note-1) He was educated at [Manchester Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Grammar_School "Manchester Grammar School")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Powell#cite_note-independ310-2) (which was then a [direct grant grammar school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_grant_grammar_school "Direct grant grammar school")), and studied law at the [University of Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Manchester "University of Manchester"). He has an elder brother.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Powell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Powell began acting at school, playing the title role in Shakespeare's _King Lear_. He also appeared as a teenager in _The Adventures of Samuel Poppleton_ on BBC Radio Children's Hour from the North of England in Manchester, where he came under the guidance of producer [Trevor Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Hill_(producer) "Trevor Hill (producer)"), as detailed in Hill's autobiography, _Over the Airwaves_. He secured a post at a repertory theatre in [Stoke-on-Trent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke-on-Trent "Stoke-on-Trent"). His first film part was in _[Robbery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbery\_(1967\_film) "Robbery (1967 film)")_ (1967), which starred [Stanley Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Baker "Stanley Baker") and was about the [Great Train Robbery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Train_Robbery_(1963) "Great Train Robbery (1963)"), in which he played the second man or locomotive driver's assistant. He had a small role in the original film version of _[The Italian Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Italian\_Job "The Italian Job")_ (1969) playing one of the gang, but had to wait a few years for his first success, playing scientist Toby Wren in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")'s [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction") series _[Doomwatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doomwatch "Doomwatch")_ in 1970.

Having been killed off in _Doomwatch_ right at the end of Series One in a bomb explosion, at his request, Powell became a pin-up and a household name, following up with starring roles in several BBC serials, including television adaptations of the novels _[Sentimental Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental\_Education "Sentimental Education")_ (1970) and _[Jude the Obscure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude\_the\_Obscure\_(TV\_serial,\_1971) "Jude the Obscure (TV serial, 1971)")_ (1971). In 1972–1973 he portrayed [Charles Rolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Rolls "Charles Rolls") in the miniseries _[The Edwardians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Edwardians\_(miniseries) "The Edwardians (miniseries)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Powell#cite_note-3) He starred in 1973 in the first episode of the British series _[Thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller\_(British\_TV\_series) "Thriller (British TV series)")_. He also appeared in the 1975 series _[Looking for Clancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looking\_for\_Clancy "Looking for Clancy")_, based on the [Frederic Mullally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederic_Mullally "Frederic Mullally") novel _Clancy_. For several years Powell continued as a television regular, with occasional forays into film, as the Austrian composer [Gustav Mahler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_Mahler "Gustav Mahler") in the [Ken Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Russell "Ken Russell")[biopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopic "Biopic")_[Mahler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler\_(film) "Mahler (film)")_ (1974) and Captain Walker in Russell's film version of _[Tommy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy\_(1975\_film) "Tommy (1975 film)")_ (1975). His role in _Tommy_ had few lines, speaking only during the overture with [Ann-Margret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann-Margret "Ann-Margret"), he is primarily seen through the mind of his son as played by Barry Winch (Young Tommy) and [Roger Daltrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Daltrey "Roger Daltrey").

**Sir Roger Harry Daltrey** (born 1 March 1944) is an English singer, songwriter and actor. He is the co-founder and lead vocalist of the [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who"), known for his powerful voice and charismatic stage presence.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Daltrey#cite_note-Susan-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Daltrey#cite_note-Franklin,_Gregory-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Daltrey#cite_note-3) His stage persona earned him a position as one of the "gods of rock and roll".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Daltrey#cite_note-Franklin,_Gregory-2)

Daltrey's hit songs with the Who include "[My Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Generation "My Generation")", "[Pinball Wizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinball_Wizard "Pinball Wizard")", "[Won't Get Fooled Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Won't_Get_Fooled_Again "Won't Get Fooled Again")", "[Baba O'Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baba_O'Riley "Baba O'Riley")", "[Who Are You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who_Are_You_(The_Who_song) "Who Are You (The Who song)")" and "[You Better You Bet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Better_You_Bet "You Better You Bet")". He began a solo career in 1973 while still a member of the Who, and has released ten solo studio albums, five compilation albums and one live album. His solo hits include "[Giving It All Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giving_It_All_Away "Giving It All Away")", "[Free Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Me_(Roger_Daltrey_song) "Free Me (Roger Daltrey song)")", "[Without Your Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Without_Your_Love_(Roger_Daltrey_song) "Without Your Love (Roger Daltrey song)")", "[Walking in My Sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walking_in_My_Sleep "Walking in My Sleep")", "[After the Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_the_Fire_(song) "After the Fire (song)")" and "[Under a Raging Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_a_Raging_Moon_(song) "Under a Raging Moon (song)")".

The Who are considered one of the most influential rock bands of the 20th century and have sold over 100 million records worldwide. As a member of the band, Daltrey received a [Lifetime achievement award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_achievement_award "Lifetime achievement award") from the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") in 1988,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Daltrey#cite_note-BPI-4) and from the Grammy Foundation in 2001.[[5]](

**Gwyllyn Samuel Newton Ford** (May 1, 1916 – August 30, 2006), known as **Glenn Ford**, was a Canadian-born American actor. He was most prominent during [Hollywood's Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_Hollywood_cinema "Classical Hollywood cinema") as one of the biggest box-office draws of the 1940s, 1950s, and 1960s, and had a career that lasted more than 50 years.

[![Image 5: Film: Shree 420 (1955) IMDb: 7.9/10 Duration: 2h 48m Directed by: Raj Kapoor Starring: Raj Kapoor, Nargis, Naidra, others. Music director: Shankar Jaikishan Produced by: Raj Kapoor . . "Ramaiya Vastavaiya" is a classic song from the 1955 Bollywood film Shree 420, sung by Lata Mangeshkar, Mohammed Rafi, and Mukesh. Music is by Shankar-Jaikishan and lyrics by Shailendra. "Ramaiya Vastavaiya" means "Ram, won’t you come?" it’s a Telugu phrase Shailendra picked up from a waiter in Khandala and worked into the song. In the film it’s picturised on Raj Kapoor and Nargis as they sing about giving their hearts away, contrasting pure love with the materialism and heartbreak they see around them. The mix of Rafi, Lata, and Mukesh’s voices, over Shankar-Jaikishan’s lively tune, made it an instant evergreen. Shree 420 is a Raj Kapoor film where he plays Ranbir Raj, an orphan who comes to Bombay to make it big. He falls for Vidya, a schoolteacher played by Nargis, but gets pulled into the world of a corrupt industrialist. The film contrasts idealism with the "420" culture of fraud and shortcuts in post-independence India. It was a huge hit, known for its social commentary, and gave us songs like Mera Joota Hai Japani, Pyar Hua Iqrar Hua, and Ramaiya Vastavaiya. . . Music is by Shankar-Jaikishan and lyrics by Shailendra. "Ramaiya Vastavaiya" means "Ram, won’t you come?" it’s a Telugu phrase Shailendra picked up from a waiter in Khandala and worked into the song. In the film it’s picturised on Raj Kapoor and Nargis as they sing about giving their hearts away, contrasting pure love with the materialism and heartbreak they see around them. The mix of Rafi, Lata, and Mukesh’s voices, over Shankar-Jaikishan’s lively tune, made it an instant evergreen. Shree 420 is a Raj Kapoor film where he plays Ranbir Raj, an orphan who comes to Bombay to make it big. He falls for Vidya, a schoolteacher played by Nargis, but gets pulled into the world of a corrupt industrialist. The film contrasts idealism with the "420" culture of fraud and shortcuts in post-independence India. It was a huge hit, known for its social commentary, and gave us songs like Mera Joota Hai Japani, Pyar Hua Iqrar Hua, and Ramaiya Vastavaiya. . . [![Image 17: “Baaghon Mein Bahaar Hai” — Aradhana (1969) “Baaghon Mein Bahaar Hai” is a beautiful romantic duet from the classic Bollywood film Aradhana, starring Rajesh Khanna and Sharmila Tagore. 🌸 Song Details Song: Baaghon Mein Bahaar Hai (बागों में बहार है) Movie: Aradhana (1969) Singers: Lata Mangeshkar & Mohammed Rafi Music: S. D. Burman Lyrics: Anand Bakshi Genre: Romantic On-screen: Rajesh Khanna and Sharmila Tagore 💕 Meaning & Theme The title “Baaghon Mein Bahaar Hai” literally means “There is spring in the gardens.” The blooming gardens and flowers are used as a metaphor for the blossoming of love. 🌷 The song is structured like a playful conversation between two lovers. One asks whether the other is in love, while the other teasingly denies it despite clearly showing signs of affection. American musician and actor (born 1949)

| Spouses | * [Goldie Hawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldie_Hawn "Goldie Hawn") ​ ​ (m.1976;div.1982)​ * [Cindy Williams](link_4) ​ ​ (m.1982;div.2000)​ |

**William Louis Hudson Jr.**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-1) (born October 17, 1949)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-filmref-2) is an American musician and actor. He was a vocalist in [the Hudson Brothers](link_10), a band he formed in 1965 with his two younger brothers, [Brett](link_8) and [Mark](link_7). He later had a brief acting career, appearing in supporting roles in _[Zero to Sixty](link_11)_ (1978), _[Hysterical](link_12)_ (1983), and _[Big Shots](link_13)_ (1987). He also had a recurring guest role on the series _[Doogie Howser, M.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doogie\_Howser,\_M.D [link_14]. "Doogie Howser, M.D.")_ on [ABC](link_15).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bill_Hudson_(singer)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Hudson was born and raised in [Portland, Oregon](link_3),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-filmref-2) the eldest of three sons (Brett and Mark are his two younger brothers) born to Eleanor Salerno and William Louis Hudson. His mother was of [Italian](link_16) descent; his maternal grandfather came from [Fagnano Castello](link_17), [Cosenza](link_18), [Calabria](link_19), [Italy](link_20).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-itru-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-upl-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-feht-5) He and his brothers were nephews (by marriage) of actor [Keenan Wynn](link_21).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-detroit-6)

Bill Hudson's father left his family when Hudson was around six years old, saying he was going out for a pack of cigarettes.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman201130-7) Bill's mother had to depend on [welfare](link_22) to support her children.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-act-8) He and his siblings grew up in his mother's [Catholic](link_23) faith.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman201131,_57-9)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bill_Hudson_(singer)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Bill Hudson was the vocalist for [The Hudson Brothers](link_10). As an actor, Hudson appeared in the film _[Big Shots](link_13)_ (1987), and three episodes of the television series _[Doogie Howser, M.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doogie\_Howser,\_M.D [link_14]. "Doogie Howser, M.D.")_ from 1989 to 1992.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Hudson published a memoir, _Two Versions: The Other Side of Fame and Family_, in December 2011.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-10)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bill_Hudson_(singer)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

During his bachelor days, Hudson had relationships with singer [Karen Carpenter](link_24)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman2011195-11) in addition to actresses [Loretta Swit](link_25)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman201144-12) and [Jill St. John](link_26).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman201145-13) In 1975 he and [Goldie Hawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldie_Hawn "Goldie Hawn") dated; they married in 1976. Hudson filed for divorce in 1980[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-14) and it was finalized right before he remarried in 1982.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman2011114-15) They had two children, [Oliver](link_5) and [Kate](link_6), who grew up with Hawn and [Kurt Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Russell "Kurt Russell"). When Oliver criticized his biological father in a public statement on [Father's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father [link_27]'s_Day "Father's Day") in 2015, Hudson spoke out for the first time to accuse Hawn of "willfully alienating" him from their children through the years.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-us-16)

Hudson next had a relationship with [Ali MacGraw](link_28), which dissolved by mid-1981.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman201184,_167-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-18) His second marriage was in 1982 to [Cindy Williams](link_4), with whom he had two children. They divorced in 2000.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudsonSmitherman2011204-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer)#cite_note-20) In 2006, Hudson

**Kostas** "**Gus**" **Tritchonis** (born November 21, 1937) is a Greek-American actor, dancer, and director.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gus_Trikonis&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Trikonis began his career as an actor and dancer, notably appearing in the 1961 film _[West Side Story](link_3)_ as Indio, one of the "Sharks",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Trikonis#cite_note-Film_Reference-1) as well as dancing with [Debbie Reynolds](link_4) and [Grover Dale](link_5) to the frantic "He's My Friend" in 1964's _[The Unsinkable Molly Brown](link_6)_. Although originally unbilled, on December 3, 1968, Trikonis got his second biggest exposure in front of any audience (the first being in the aforementioned _West Side Story_) as one of two main (out of five) male dancers who do [Elvis Presley](link_7)'s choreography as he sings a Gospel medley as part of a widely watched NBC-TV Special entitled "Elvis".

As a director, Trikonis handled several projects from the late 1960s to the early 1980s, mostly low-budget "[exploitation films](link_8)". He made several films for [Roger Corman](link_9) at [New World Pictures](link_10); Corman called Trikonis one of the best young directors he had ever worked with.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Trikonis#cite_note-2) His films included _[The Student Body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Student\_Body\_(1976\_film)?action=edit&redlink=1 "The Student Body (1976 film) (page does not exist)")_.

From the 1980s to the mid-1990s Trikonis mostly directed television series. He directed episodes of television series including _[Baywatch](link_11)_, _[The Flash](link_12)_, _[Quantum Leap](link_13)_, _[Hunter](link_14)_, _[Beauty and the Beast](link_15)_ and _[Wiseguy](link_16)_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Trikonis#cite_note-Film_Reference-1)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gus_Trikonis&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Trikonis was married to actress [Goldie Hawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldie_Hawn "Goldie Hawn") from 1969 to 1976; he was her first husband and they have the same birthday (in different years). He was later married to [costume designer](link_17) Barbara Andrews from 1978 until her death in 2012 and they had one child together: a son Nicolas, born in 1981.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Trikonis#cite_note-3) His sister Gina also appeared in _West Side Story_ as Graziella, Riff's girlfriend,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Trikonis#cite_note-4) later becoming a costumer and costume/wardrobe supervisor.

**[Kurt Vogel Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt%20Russell "w:Kurt Russell")** (17 March 1951) is an American actor and producer.

## Quotes

[[edit](https://en.wikiquote.org/w/index.php?title=Kurt_Russell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Quotes")]

*   Staying away from Hollywood didn't take much of an effort, there is a whole world in Los Angeles that's based on maneuvering. You say the right thing in interviews, you say yes to the right events and charities, and if you do it correctly you become someone they talk about. You become a player in the system and you're looked at as a professional, or dedicated, or whatever. You become a part of their thing, and they become part of yours... It's a wild web that can be weaved and there are people who love, love, love to play that game. And I'm not putting it down. But for me, it's just like pulling teeth. I just could never do it. 
    *   [Kurt Russell on 'Deepwater Horizon,' Hollywood and more](http://www.nj.com/entertainment/index.ssf/2016/09/kurt_russell_on_deepwater_horizon_hollywood_and_mo.html) (September 23, 2016)

*   This is a business that’s heavily promulgated by people who have a politically liberal bent. I don’t begrudge them that. I’m a libertarian; frankly, I think my liberalness goes far beyond theirs in a lot of ways. But yeah, we think differently, and maybe that’s cut me out of some things. I don’t care. People know I get along great with all kinds of directors, all kinds of actors. And I tell you, you hire me, I will show up, 24/7, and I will give you 100%. I will help you fix whatever problems come up. You hire me, I’m your boy. It’s just, it’s all about the work. And when that’s done, I am done. 
    *   [Kurt Russell on 'Deepwater Horizon,' Hollywood and more](http://www.nj.com/entertainment/index.ssf/2016/09/kurt_russell_on_deepwater_horizon_hollywood_and_mo.html) (September 23, 2016)

**Oliver Rutledge Hudson** (born September 7, 1976)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Hudson#cite_note-biography.com-1) is an American actor. He is known for his roles as Adam Rhodes in the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") comedy series _[Rules of Engagement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rules\_of\_Engagement\_(TV\_series) "Rules of Engagement (TV series)")_ (2007–2013), Jeff Fordham on the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") musical drama series _[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville\_(2012\_TV\_series) "Nashville (2012 TV series)")_ (2013–2015) and Wes Gardner in the [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") horror comedy _[Scream Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream\_Queens\_(2015\_TV\_series) "Scream Queens (2015 TV series)")_ (2015–2016). He appeared as one of the main cast members of the ABC [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom")_[Splitting Up Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splitting\_Up\_Together "Splitting Up Together")_ (2018–2019), produced by [Ellen DeGeneres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellen_DeGeneres "Ellen DeGeneres"). In 2022, he played [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI "FBI") agent Garrett Miller in Fox's _[The Cleaning Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cleaning\_Lady\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Cleaning Lady (American TV series)")_.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oliver_Hudson&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Hudson was born in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award")-winning actress [Goldie Hawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldie_Hawn "Goldie Hawn") and musician [Bill Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hudson_(singer) "Bill Hudson (singer)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Hudson#cite_note-biography.com-1) After his parents divorced in 1980, he and his sister, actress [Kate Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Hudson "Kate Hudson"), were raised in [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") by their mother and her partner, actor [Kurt Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Russell "Kurt Russell"). He has four half-siblings: Emily and Zachary, from his biological father's marriage to actress [Cindy Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams "Cindy Williams"); Lalania, from another of his father's relationships in 2006; and [Wyatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyatt_Russell "Wyatt Russell"), from his mother's relationship with Kurt Russell. He also has a step-sibling, Boston, from Kurt Russell's marriage to Season Hubley.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Hudson#cite_note-2)

Hudson is of [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_American "Italian American") descent via his father; [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Americans "English Americans") and [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Americans "German Americans") descent through his maternal grandfather, and [Hungarian Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Hungary "History of the Jews in Hungary") descent through his maternal grandmother.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Hudson#cite_note-Irish-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Hudson#cite_note-itru-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Hudson#cite_note-5)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oliver_Hudson&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Hudson appeared opposite his mother in the 1999 comedy film _[The Out-of-Towners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Out-of-Towners\_(1999\_film) "The Out-of-Towners (1999 film)")_ and later starred in several teen movies, such as _[The Smokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Smokers\_(film) "The Smokers (film)")_ and _[Going Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Going\_Greek "Going Greek")_. In 2002, he played the lead role of [The WB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_WB_Television_Network "The WB Television Network") comedy series _[My Guide to Becoming a Rock Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Guide\_to\_Becoming\_a\_Rock\_Star "My Guide to Becoming a Rock Star")_. Hudson also appeared in a recurring role opposite [Katie Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Holmes "Katie Holmes") as her love interest, Eddie Doling, in sixteen episodes of _[Dawson's Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawson's\_Creek "Dawson's Creek")_ from 2002 to 2003.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Hudson#cite_note-6)

Hudson starred in The WB series _[The Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mountain\_(TV\_series) "The Mountain (TV series)")_ from 2004 to 2005; the show was canceled after 13 episodes. In 2006, he starred in horror films _[The Breed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Breed\_(2006\_film) "The Breed (2006 film)")_ and _[Black Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Christmas\_(2006\_film) "Black Christmas (2006 film)")_. _**Nashville Girl**_ is a 1976 film from [New World Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_World_Pictures "New World Pictures") about an aspiring country and western singer.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Girl#cite_note-1)

It was also known as _New Girl in Town_ and _Country Music Daughter_ to capitalize on the success of the similar film _[Coal Miner's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal\_Miner's\_Daughter\_(film) "Coal Miner's Daughter (film)")_.

Roger Corman says the film was very popular in the South and also in Europe, which surprised him.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Girl#cite_note-2)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nashville_Girl&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Jamie, a 16 year old [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer, runs away from home to try to become a star, only to find herself being sexually manipulated and exploited by older men in the country music business.

*   [Johnny Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Rodriguez "Johnny Rodriguez") as Himself
*   [Jesse White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_White_(actor) "Jesse White (actor)") as C.Y. Ordell
*   Marcie Barkin as Alice
*   [Shirley Jo Finney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_Jo_Finney "Shirley Jo Finney") as Frisky
*   [Judith Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judith_Roberts_(actress) "Judith Roberts (actress)") as Fran
*   [Leo Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leo_Gordon "Leo Gordon") as Burt

**Season Hubley** (born March 14, 1951) is an American retired actress, best known as Nikki in _[Hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore\_(1979\_film) "Hardcore (1979 film)")_ (1979), [Priscilla Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priscilla_Presley "Priscilla Presley") in _[Elvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis\_(1979\_film) "Elvis (1979 film)")_ (1979), and Angelique in _[All My Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_My\_Children "All My Children")_ (1992–1994).

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Season_Hubley&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Hubley was steadily active, in film, and on television, from her first 1972 appearance in the eponymous lead role in the television film _Bobby Jo and the Good Time Band_,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_Hubley#cite_note-BobbyJo-2) through to her final 1999 appearance in a guest-starring role on the episode ["Wreck of the Zephyr"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Flipper_(1995_TV_series)_episodes#ep62 "List of Flipper (1995 TV series) episodes") of the television series _[Flipper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flipper\_(1995\_TV\_series) "Flipper (1995 TV series)")_.

In television, she made an appearance on _[The Partridge Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Partridge\_Family "The Partridge Family")_ in 1972 playing the part of a princess. In 1977, she appeared in an episode of _[Kojak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kojak "Kojak")_ as a nun whose sister was murdered.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_Hubley#cite_note-TVGuide-3) She had a continuing role in the evening TV drama _[Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family\_(1976\_TV\_series) "Family (1976 TV series)")_, guest-starring in several episodes in 1976 and 1977 as Salina Magee, the love interest of teenage dropout Willie Lawrence.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_Hubley#cite_note-TVGuide-3) She also co-starred in an episode of _[Starsky & Hutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starsky\_&\_Hutch "Starsky & Hutch")_, "Starsky's Lady", in which she was Starsky's fiancée.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_Hubley#cite_note-TVGuide-3) From 1991 to 1994, she portrayed Angelique Marick on the daytime drama _[All My Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_My\_Children "All My Children")_. She appeared in _[Stepfather III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepfather\_III "Stepfather III")_ and _[Child in the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child\_in\_the\_Night "Child in the Night")_, both in 1990.

Hubley appeared in a mix of supporting and lead roles through the 1970s. In 1973, she played the title character in _[Lolly-Madonna XXX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolly-Madonna\_XXX "Lolly-Madonna XXX")_, also known as _The Lolly Madonna War_, around whom the story revolved.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_Hubley#cite_note-evnw850505-4) She co-starred in the 1979 film _[Hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore\_(1979\_film) "Hardcore (1979 film)")_. She appeared briefly in _[Escape from New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape\_from\_New\_York "Escape from New York")_ (1981), with her husband [Kurt Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Russell "Kurt Russell"). Her other major film role is in the 1982 cult film _[Vice Squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice\_Squad\_(1982\_film) "Vice Squad (1982 film)")_, in which she played a prostitute named Princess. A notable role for Hubley was her lead performance as [Priscilla Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priscilla_Presley "Priscilla Presley") in the 1979 made-for-television film _[Elvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis\_(1979\_film) "Elvis (1979 film)")_.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Season_Hubley&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Hubley was married to actor [Kurt Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Russell "Kurt Russell") from 1979 to 1983. They have a son named Boston (b. February 16, 1980).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_Hubley#cite_note-5)

**Cynthia Jane Williams** (August 22, 1947– January 25, 2023) was an American actress. She is best known for her role as Shirley Feeney on the television sitcoms _[Happy Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy\_Days "Happy Days")_ (1975–1979), and _[Laverne & Shirley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laverne\_&\_Shirley "Laverne & Shirley")_ (1976–1982). She also appeared in _[American Graffiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Graffiti "American Graffiti")_ (1973), _[The Conversation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Conversation "The Conversation")_ (1974), _[Mr. Ricco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_Ricco "Mr. Ricco")_ (1975), and _[More American Graffiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/More\_American\_Graffiti "More American Graffiti")_ (1979).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cindy_Williams&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Williams was born in [Van Nuys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Nuys "Van Nuys"), Los Angeles on August 22, 1947. Her mother, Cindy, was a waitress and her father, Beachard "Bill" Williams, worked at an electronics manufacturing company.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-2) The family moved to [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas") when she was a year old and returned to Los Angeles when she was ten years old.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-emmytvlegends-3) She had a sister named Carol Ann.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Williams wrote and acted at a church during childhood and later acted in productions at [Birmingham High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_High_School "Birmingham High School"); she graduated in 1965, a year behind [Sally Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sally_Field "Sally Field"). She attended [Los Angeles City College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_City_College "Los Angeles City College") where she majored in theater.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-emmytvlegends-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cindy_Williams&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After college, Williams began her professional career by landing national commercials, which included [Foster Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foster_Grant "Foster Grant") sunglasses and [TWA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TWA "TWA").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-emmytvlegends-3) Her first roles in television, among others, were on _[Room 222](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room\_222 "Room 222")_,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-emmytvlegends-3)_[Nanny and the Professor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanny\_and\_the\_Professor "Nanny and the Professor")_, and _[Love, American Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love,\_American\_Style "Love, American Style")_.

Williams accompanied an actor-friend from [Los Angeles City College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_City_College "Los Angeles City College") who needed a scene partner for the audition and was also accepted at [The Actors Studio West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Actors_Studio_West "The Actors Studio West"), but rarely attended due to acting commitments.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-emmytvlegends-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-:0-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-5) Williams picked up important film roles early in her career: [George Cukor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Cukor "George Cukor")'s _[Travels with My Aunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travels\_with\_My\_Aunt\_(film) "Travels with My Aunt (film)")_ (1972); as Laurie Henderson, [Ron Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Howard "Ron Howard")'s character's high school sweetheart in [George Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lucas "George Lucas")'s _[American Graffiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Graffiti "American Graffiti")_ (1973) for which she earned a [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") nomination as Best Supporting Actress;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-6) and [Francis Ford Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ford_Coppola "Francis Ford Coppola")'s _[The Conversation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Conversation "The Conversation")_ (1974). She auditioned along with thousands of others, for Lucas's _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars\_(film) "Star Wars (film)")_ for the role of [Princess Leia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Leia "Princess Leia"), but Leia was ultimately played by [Carrie Fisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrie_Fisher "Carrie Fisher") because Lucas wished to cast unknowns, as in _American Graffiti_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Williams#cite_note-8)

Williams met [Penny Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Marshall "Penny Marshall"), first on a double date, and later at [Francis Ford Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ford_Coppola "Francis Ford Coppola")'s

_**Zero to Sixty**_ is a 1978 American [comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film") directed by [Don Weis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Weis "Don Weis") and starring [Darren McGavin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_McGavin "Darren McGavin"), [Sylvia Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_Miles "Sylvia Miles"), [Joan Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Collins "Joan Collins"), [Denise Nickerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denise_Nickerson "Denise Nickerson"), and [Dick Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Martin_(comedian) "Dick Martin (comedian)"). The film was released on June 23, 1978,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero_to_Sixty#cite_note-1) and was later reviewed by _TV Guide_, which called [Darren McGavin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_McGavin "Darren McGavin") "fun to watch" in the film, but noted the premise was brought to the screen six years later in a different film, _[Repo Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repo\_Man\_(film) "Repo Man (film)")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero_to_Sixty#cite_note-2)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zero_to_Sixty&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Michael Nolan (McGavin) finds himself down on his luck following his divorce settlement, which has left him with nothing. During the repossession of his car, he makes chase all the way to the auto repossession company. His persistence impresses the owner, who hires him on the spot. Nolan is then teamed up with Larry, a 16-year-old experienced repo agent. As Nolan settles into his new career, he continually finds himself troubled by women, angry car owners, and more.

_**Touched by Love**_ (originally titled _**To Elvis, With Love**_) is a 1980 American film directed by [Gus Trikonis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Trikonis "Gus Trikonis"), starring [Diane Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Lane "Diane Lane") and [Deborah Raffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deborah_Raffin "Deborah Raffin").

First released to theaters in April 1980,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touched_by_Love#cite_note-3) the film was based on the book _To Elvis, With Love_ by the real-life therapist, Lena Canada, in which she presented the correspondence between her patient Karen Brown and [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley") as true.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Touched_by_Love&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Therapist Lena Canada tries a novel approach with a girl named Karen Brown, who is dealing with [cerebral palsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_palsy "Cerebral palsy") and [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_(mood) "Depression (mood)"). She encourages Karen to write to her favorite singer [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"). Karen eventually receives a reply, and they become [pen pals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pen_pals "Pen pals"). The interaction leads to an immediate improvement in her daily outlook.

[![Image 9: One of the most unforgettable scenes in The Nun’s Story (1959). Director Fred Zinnemann saved the haircut scene for the very last day of filming. _**The Sidehackers**_ (also known as _**Five the Hard Way**_) is a 1969 American [action film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film") about motorcycle racing with a twist. Each motorcycle has a sidehack (a [sidecar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidecar "Sidecar") with a rail but no sidewalls or seat), in which a passenger rides and tilts to one side or the other when going around curves. The credits thank the "Southern California Sidehack Association"; sidehacking is also known as [sidecarcross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidecarcross "Sidecarcross") or "sidecar motocross racing".

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Sidehackers&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Rommel is a mechanic at a motorbike repair shop who works alongside his partner Luke, and competes in sidehack-style races. He and his fiancée Rita plan to get married soon. Rommel meets J.C., a hot-tempered entertainer, when he brings his bike in for repair. J.C. sees a sidehack bike in the shop and takes a liking to it. Rommel invites J.C. and his crew to join him in a sidehack event the upcoming weekend. At the event, J.C. enjoys watching Rommel race on the sidehack; J.C. later accepts a ride on a sidehack at a cabin Rommel shares with his girlfriend, Rita.

A day of racing on Rommel's sidehack is followed by a dinner party at the cabin. The party turns ugly when Rommel declines to join his J.C.'s gang. J.C. loses his temper when Dirty John (one of his henchmen) asks him a question and Nero (another henchman) tries to calm him. After J.C. again asks Rommel to join his gang, J.C.'s girlfriend, Paisley, reminds him that Rommel isn't interested. Infuriated by her comment, J.C. reluctantly accepts Rommel's rejection and everyone awkwardly walks out of the cabin.

Angry with Paisley, J.C. pressures her into answering why Rommel shouldn't join their crew. Paisley finds it humorous, and tells J.C. that she finds him disappointing. When she tries to leave, J.C. roughly pulls her back. J.C. tells her to scream for help; when she does, J.C. punches her in the stomach, and tells her she is his and no one else's.

The next day, while Rommel and Luke are working on a bike, Paisley comes over and tries to seduce Rommel, but he rejects her. When J.C. and his men return to their hotel, they find a drunk and disheveled Paisley, who claims that Rommel raped her. Angered, J.C. and his gang find Rommel and Rita in their cabin making love. The gang beat Rommel unconscious, then rape Rita, killing her in the process. Luke finds Rommel and Rita, and calls the police. Now a wanted man, J.C. is forced into hiding.

Despite Luke's warnings to let the police handle the situation, Rommel is determined get revenge. Rommel gathers a hit squad that consists of J.C.'s former henchmen Nero, muscle-bound Big Jake, bailed-out criminal Crapout, and Cooch (who is a double agent for J.C.). With help from Cooch, Rommel and his gang head out into the canyons where J.C. is known to be hiding; Luke goes after Rommel to stop him. Rommel's plan involves engaging J.C. and his gang in hand-to-hand combat. Suspecting J.C.'s gang may be armed, Rommel's gang reluctantly agrees to the plan.

The next morning, Cooch sneaks over to J.C.'s hideout and advises him on Rommel's plan. After Cooch leaves, J.C. celebrates his victory with Paisley, thinking his victory over Rommel is all but certain. Paisley breaks up with J.C. because of his abuse as well as her guilt for indirectly causing Rita's death. An enraged J.C. strangles Paisley to death, and then apologizes to her corpse, chiding her for making him so angry.

Luke tries to talk Rommel out of his retribution, telling Rommel that he is no better than J.C. if he follows through; Rommel ignores Luke's pleas. Rommel's gang catches Cooch returning from J.C.'s camp. After the gang savagely beats him, Cooch reveals that J.C. can be found in a rock quarry in the canyons. Finally realizing revenge is worthless, Rommel asks Luke to tell the police where J.C. is hiding. Rommel's men attack J.C. in his hideout. Big Jake is shot and killed after taking down two of J.C.'s men. Cooch manages to escape and runs to J.C., who kills him for his betrayal. Nero and Crapout escape on a bike as the latter shoots the rest of J.C.'s men.

Rommel and J.C. find each other in the quarry and fight. Rommel manages to gain the upper hand, but when the police arrive he decides to walk away. J.C. finds a gun dropped by one of his dead henchmen and shoots Rommel in the back. The film concludes with a flashback of Rommel and Rita rolling about in a grassy field, superimposed over a shot of Rommel's dead body.

## _Mystery Science Theater 3000_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Sidehackers&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mystery Science Theater 3000")]

On September 29, 1990, _The Sidehackers_ was featured on _[Mystery Science Theater 3000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery\_Science\_Theater\_3000 "Mystery Science Theater 3000")_ (MST3K) in episode #202. It includes one of the few occasions [Cambot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambot "Cambot") actually interacts with the experiment other than simply filming it; in this case, the bot places an [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")-like score graphic during the movie's racing sequences.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sidehackers#cite_note-1)

The episode was released on DVD by [Rhino Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhino_Entertainment "Rhino Entertainment") as part of the third volume of the _Mystery Science Theater 3000_ DVD box sets. The four-disc collection was later reissued by [Shout Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shout_Factory "Shout Factory") in September 2016.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sidehackers#cite_note-2)

### Edits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Sidehackers&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Edits")]

The MST3K writers were initially unaware of the film's darker content when they selected it for the show, only having watched the entirety of the film during the writing process. They were horrified to discover the scene in which Rommel's girlfriend Rita is raped and killed, juxtaposed with shots of Luke and Lois' children playfully roughhousing. This scene, and the discovery of Rita's nearly nude body, were removed from the episode. To make up for the missing plot elements, the character of [Crow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crow_T._Robot "Crow T. Robot") interposes, "For those of you playing along at home, Rita is dead." According to the series' [head writer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_writer "Head writer") (and future host) [Michael J. Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_J._Nelson "Michael J. Nelson"), "We were all traumatized, the scene got cut, and from that day forward, movies were watched in their entirety (for such potentially offensive content) before they were selected."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sidehackers#cite_note-3)
