Wikipedia's editing interface

Although changes are not systematically reviewed, Wikipedia's software provides tools allowing anyone to review changes made by others. Each article's History page links to each revision.[h][108] On most articles, anyone can view the latest changes and undo others' revisions by clicking a link on the article's History page. Registered users may maintain a "watchlist" of articles that interest them so they can be notified of changes.[109] There are a variety of different 'patrols' on Wikipedia,[110] including "New pages patrol" a patrol where newly created articles are checked for glaring issues.[111]

In 2003, economics PhD student Andrea Ciffolilli argued that the low transaction costs of participating in a wiki created a catalyst for collaborative development, and that features such as allowing easy access to past versions of a page favored "creative construction" over "creative destruction".[112]

Vandalism
Main article: Vandalism on Wikipedia

Any change that deliberately compromises Wikipedia's integrity is considered vandalism. The most common and obvious types of vandalism include additions of obscenities and crude humor, but it can also include advertising and other types of spam.[113] Sometimes editors commit vandalism by removing content or entirely blanking a given page. Less common types of vandalism, such as the deliberate addition of plausible but false information, can be more difficult to detect. Vandals can introduce irrelevant formatting, modify page semantics such as the page's title or categorization, manipulate the article's underlying code, or use images disruptively.[114]

Obvious vandalism is generally easy to remove from Wikipedia articles; the median time to detect and fix it is a few minutes.[115][116] However, some vandalism takes much longer to detect and repair.[117]

In the Seigenthaler biography incident, an anonymous editor introduced false information into the biography of American political figure John Seigenthaler in May 2005, falsely presenting him as a suspect in the assassination of John F. Kennedy.[117] It remained uncorrected for four months.[117] Seigenthaler, the founding editorial director of USA Today and founder of the Freedom Forum First Amendment Center at Vanderbilt University, called Wikipedia co-founder Jimmy Wales and asked whether he had any way of knowing who contributed the misinformation. Wales said he did not, although the perpetrator was eventually traced.[118][119] After the incident, Seigenthaler described Wikipedia as "a flawed and irresponsible research tool".[117] The incident led to policy changes at Wikipedia for tightening up the verifiability of biographical articles of living people.[120]

Disputes and edit warring
Main article: Disputes on Wikipedia

Wikipedia editors often have disagreements regarding content, which can be discussed on article Talk pages. Disputes may result in repeated competing changes to an article, known as "edit warring".[121][122] It is widely seen as a resource-consuming scenario where no useful knowledge is added,[123] and criticized as creating a competitive[124] and conflict-based editing culture associated with traditional masculine gender roles.[125][126] Research has focused on, for example, impoliteness of disputes,[127][128] the influence of rival editing camps,[129][130] the conversational structure,[131] and the shift in conflicts to a focus on sources.[132][133]

Taha Yasseri of the University of Oxford examined editing conflicts and their resolution in a 2013 study.[134][135] Yasseri contended that simple reverts or "undo" operations were not the most significant measure of counterproductive work behavior at Wikipedia. **Meenakshi Seshadri Mysore** (pronounced[[miːnaːkʂiː ʃeːʂaːdrɪ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); [née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%A9e "Née")**Seshadri**; born 16 November 1963) as Shashikala Seshadri, is an Indian former actress and beauty pageant titleholder who worked primarily in [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi"), [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") and [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") films. Seshadri established herself as one of the most popular and highest-paid actresses of the late 1980s and early 1990s and is considered among the leading actresses of [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema").[[1]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-1)

Prior to her acting career, Seshadri won the Eve's Weekly [Miss India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femina_Miss_India#History "Femina Miss India") contest in 1981 at the age of 17.[[2]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-Zeearticle-2)[[3]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-3) She became one of Hindi cinema's leading actresses in the 1980s and 1990s, and was acknowledged for several of her performances, her beauty, and her accomplished dancing.[[4]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-4) She made her debut with the film _[Painter Babu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Painter\_Babu "Painter Babu")_ (1983) produced by [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar"), and her second film _[Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero\_(1983\_film) "Hero (1983 film)")_ (1983) catapulted her to instant stardom. ## Career

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Debut and early success (1983–1985)

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Debut and early success (1983–1985)")]

After a forgettable debut in _Painter Babu_, Meenakshi acted alongside another newcomer, [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff"), in _[Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero\_(1983\_film) "Hero (1983 film)")_. The film was a blockbuster and Meenakshi became an overnight star.[[16]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-16) Immediately after the success of _Hero_, she got an offer to star with superstar [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") to appear in a double role in _Awara Baap_ but the film underperformed at the box office. She then appeared in several commercial films, including _Love Marriage_, _Paisa Ye Paisa_, and _[Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lover\_Boy\_(1985\_film) "Lover Boy (1985 film)")._ Her next successful film was _[Bewafai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewafai "Bewafai")_, with Khanna again and starring [Rajinikanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajinikanth "Rajinikanth") as the antagonist. Then Ghai again cast her alongside [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor") in _[Meri Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meri\_Jung "Meri Jung")_, which was one of the highest-grossing films of 1985. This gave her a major foothold in the industry. _Swati_, _[Mera Jawab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mera\_Jawab "Mera Jawab")_, and _[Aandhi Toofan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aandhi\_Toofan "Aandhi Toofan")_ were all moderately successful. The same year she also appeared with [Jeetendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeetendra "Jeetendra") in _[Hoshiyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoshiyar "Hoshiyar")_ and with [Rajinikanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajinikanth "Rajinikanth") in _[Mahaguru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahaguru\_(1985\_film) "Mahaguru (1985 film)")_ (1985) as his heroine. In 1986 Meenakshi made a special appearance in a song with Rajinikanth in the Telugu movie _[Jeevana Poratam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeevana\_Poratam "Jeevana Poratam")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Established actress (1986–1989)

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Established actress (1986–1989)")]

Seshadri appeared in many critically acclaimed films in 1986. In _Swati_, a woman-centric art house film, she performed the title role. The film gained immense critical acclaim and critics said, "Meenakshi Seshadri has acted in _Swati_ the way Amitabh Bachchan acts in his films". That same year she appeared in B. R. Chopra films alongside [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff") and [Raj Babbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Babbar "Raj Babbar") in the romantic drama _[Dahleez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dahleez\_(film) "Dahleez (film)")_, which dealt with the taboo topic of infidelity but underperformed at the box office. Her other releases that year, such as _[Allah Rakha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allah\_Rakha\_(film) "Allah Rakha (film)")_, were average performers at the box office. _Dilwala_ (1986) and _[Parivaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parivaar\_(1987\_film) "Parivaar (1987 film)")_ with Mithun Chakraborty did very well at box office. _Main Balwan_ (1986) was average in India, but a superhit overseas.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1987, she appeared in the hit film _[Inaam Dus Hazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inaam\_Dus\_Hazaar "Inaam Dus Hazaar")_ alongside [Sanjay Dutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Dutt "Sanjay Dutt"). She also appeared in _[Dacait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacait "Dacait")_, an action drama alongside [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol") to critical acclaim.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1988, she starred in [Yash Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra")'s multi-starrer _[Vijay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay\_(1988\_film) "Vijay (1988 film)")_. She also starred in the much hyped _[Shahenshah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahenshah\_(1988\_film) "Shahenshah (1988 film)")_ opposite Amitabh Bachchan which proved to be a huge success.[[4]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-4) Meenakshi teamed up with Bachchan for _Toofan_, _Akayla_, and _[Gangaa Jamunaa Saraswati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangaa\_Jamunaa\_Saraswati "Gangaa Jamunaa Saraswati")_, but all three were flops.

In 1988 [Prakash Mehra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakash_Mehra "Prakash Mehra") had announced _Dhan Dhahej_, starring Anil Kapoor and Meenakshi, Sanjay Khan announced _Sarzameen_ with Anil Kapoor, Meenakshi, and [Vinod Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinod_Khanna "Vinod Khanna"), [Ramesh Sippy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Sippy "Ramesh Sippy") announced _Aalishaan_ with Amitabh Bachchan and Meenakshi but none of these movies took off. Then Subhash Ghai signed Bachchan for the first time in film _[Devaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devaa "Devaa")_ opposite Meenakshi Seshadri, but it was shelved after a song picturised on Bachchan and Shammi Kapoor that was sung by [Mohammed Aziz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Aziz "Mohammed Aziz").

In 1989, she was directed by Dev Anand in _[Sachché Ká Bol-Bálá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachch%C3%A9\_K%C3%A1\_Bol-B%C3%A1l%C3%A1 "Sachché Ká Bol-Bálá")._ In 1989, she also made her Tamil film debut with _[En Rathathin Rathame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/En\_Rathathin\_Rathame "En Rathathin Rathame")_, a remake of the Hindi film _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_, opposite [K. Bhagyaraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Bhagyaraj "K. Bhagyaraj"), which bombed at the box office. She also appeared in Kalpataru's family dramas _[Bade Ghar Ki Beti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bade\_Ghar\_Ki\_Beti "Bade Ghar Ki Beti")_ and _[Gharana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gharana\_(1989\_film) "Gharana (1989 film)")_ which were moderate successes.[[4]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-4)

She worked with fellow dancer [Mithun Chakraborthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mithun_Chakraborthy "Mithun Chakraborthy") in _[Aandhi Toofan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aandhi\_Toofan "Aandhi Toofan")_, _[Main Balwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main\_Balwan "Main Balwan")_, _[Dilwaala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilwaala "Dilwaala")_, _[Parivaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parivaar\_(1987\_film) "Parivaar (1987 film)")_, _[Bees Saal Baad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bees\_Saal\_Baad\_(1988\_film) "Bees Saal Baad (1988 film)")_ _[Pyar Ka Karz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyar\_Ka\_Karz "Pyar Ka Karz")_, and _[Shandaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shandaar "Shandaar")._ Her pairings with [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff"), [Vinod Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinod_Khanna "Vinod Khanna") and [Rishi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rishi_Kapoor "Rishi Kapoor") were hugely popular and often praised by the media _.[[4]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi\_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp\_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz\_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY\_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite\_note-Boxofficeindia.com-4)[[17]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi\_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp\_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz\_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY\_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite\_note-17)_ Her best and most successful pairing, as well as her best on-screen chemistry was with Anil Kapoor. Her successful films with Anil Kapoor include _[Aag Se Khelenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aag\_Se\_Khelenge "Aag Se Khelenge")_, _Meri Jung_, _[Humlaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humlaa "Humlaa")_ and _[Ghar Ho Toh Aisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Ho\_To\_Aisa "Ghar Ho To Aisa")_, while some others like _Love Marriage_, _Amba_, _[Joshilaay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshilaay "Joshilaay")_ were box office duds.

### Commercial success (1990–1996)

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial success (1990–1996)")]

In 1990, Meenakshi appeared in two films by [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt"), the first being _Awaargi_, an art house film. Many critics call this her best performance.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The second film was _[Jurm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurm\_(1990\_film) "Jurm (1990 film)")_, released in the same year. The film was a critical and commercial success. Her role as a wife who has to face her problems after her husband gets involved with another woman gained immense critical praise. She received her first [Filmfare Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award "Filmfare Award") nomination for best actress for her role in the film. She also appeared in the film _[Ghar Ho To Aisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Ho\_To\_Aisa "Ghar Ho To Aisa")_ opposite Anil Kapoor; the film was a hit and Meenakshi was noted for her comedic timing.[[5]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-boxofficeindia1-5) She then appeared in _[Ghayal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghayal\_(1990\_film) "Ghayal (1990 film)")_ alongside [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"). This film started her long association with [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi"). _Ghayal_ was the highest-grossing film of the 1990.

In 1991, she appeared opposite Amitabh Bachchan in _[Akayla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akayla "Akayla")_, directed by [Ramesh Sippy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Sippy "Ramesh Sippy"); despite being well-promoted, the film flopped at the box office. Her on-screen pairing with Vinod Khanna was widely appreciated, and the pair starred in such successful films as _Satyamev Jayate_, _Mahaadev_, _Jurm_, _Humshakal_, and _Police Aur Mujrim_. She acted in the successful family drama _[Ghar Parivar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Parivar "Ghar Parivar")_ in 1991, with [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") and Rishi Kapoor as her co-stars. Meenakshi made her Telugu film debut with _[Brahmarshi Viswamitra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmarshi\_Viswamitra "Brahmarshi Viswamitra")_ in 1991. The same year, Raj Kumar Santoshi started the film _[Dil Hai Tumhara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Hai\_Tumhara "Dil Hai Tumhara")_ with Sunny Deol. Meenakshi paired for the first time with Salman Khan; they only shot once before the film was shelved.

In 1992, she appeared in the Telugu film _[Aapadbandhavudu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aapadbandhavudu "Aapadbandhavudu")_ opposite [Chiranjeevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiranjeevi "Chiranjeevi"). In 1992 her film _Aaj Ka Goonda Raaj_ opposite Chiranjeevi was a hit.

In 1993, she appeared in the film _[Damini – Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damini\_%E2%80%93\_Lightning "Damini – Lightning")_. Directed by filmmaker [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi"), it also starred Rishi Kapoor, Sunny Deol, [Amrish Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrish_Puri "Amrish Puri"), [Tinnu Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tinnu_Anand "Tinnu Anand"), and [Paresh Rawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paresh_Rawal "Paresh Rawal"). The film depicted the sensitive subject of injustice towards a rape victim.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] She won many accolades for her performance in the film. _Damini_ received a number of awards, including a [National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_(India) "National Film Award (India)") and a Filmfare Award nomination.[[4]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-Boxofficeindia.com-4)_Damini_ is regarded as Meenakshi's career-defining role[[18]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-bo-18) and considered a cult feminist film.[[19]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-20) She performed a [Tandav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tandav "Tandav") dance in the film, choreographed by Ravindra Atibudhi. In 1993, she also appeared in _[Aadmi Khilona Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aadmi\_Khilona\_Hai "Aadmi Khilona Hai")_ opposite [Govinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Govinda_(actor) "Govinda (actor)"); and _[Kshatriya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kshatriya "Kshatriya")_ opposite [Vinod Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinod_Khanna "Vinod Khanna") – both the films were successful at the box office.

In 1994, she appeared in the Tamil film _[Duet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duet\_(1994\_film) "Duet (1994 film)")_ opposite [Prabhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabhu_(actor) "Prabhu (actor)"), directed by [K. Balachander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Balachander "K. Balachander").[[21]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-21) The same year, she was in a dance show of songs from _[Damini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damini "Damini")_: "Bin Sajan Jhula Jholu" with Aamir Khan.

Meenakshi played the female lead in the 1996 film _[Ghatak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghatak:\_Lethal "Ghatak: Lethal")_ opposite Sunny Deol, directed by [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi"). It was one of the highest-grossing films of 1996. This was her last film, as she moved to the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") after marriage.[[6]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-boxofficeindia1996-6)[[7]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-rmrmedia1-7)

### Hiatus (1997–present)

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Hiatus (1997–present)")]

After her marriage, she made a rare appearance on [Shekhar Suman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Suman "Shekhar Suman")'s talk show.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] After a few years of marriage, she shifted her base to [Plano, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plano,_Texas "Plano, Texas"), in the United States.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In an interview she stated: "Coming from a very Indo-centric background, life abroad shook me, I just could not relate to the US environment."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] However, with the passage of time she has settled there.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Now she is running her own dance school in [Carrollton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrollton,_Texas "Carrollton, Texas") called Cherish Institute of Dance;[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The school is described as "an assembly of talented dancers, a voluntary body to enhance multi-culture, revealing the best talent of people of all ages".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Personal life

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Meenakshi retired from cinema after marrying investment banker Harish Mysore in 1995. They had a civil wedding and a registered marriage in New York.[[22]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-22) The couple have two children, a daughter and a son.[[23]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-23) Meenakshi lived in Plano, Texas.[[24]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-24) There, she taught [Bharatanatyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatanatyam "Bharatanatyam"), [Kathak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathak "Kathak"), and [Odissi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odissi "Odissi"). She performs with her students at charity events and fundraisers,[[7]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-rmrmedia1-7) including the [American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Association_of_Physicians_of_Indian_Origin "American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin") (AAPI) convention in California. She has shifted to Mumbai.[[25]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-25)

## Artistry and legacy

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Artistry and legacy")]

### Acting and dance

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Acting and dance")]

Meenakshi Sheshadri is considered one of the great actresses of Indian cinema. "Box Office India" described her as very beautiful and included her in eight top actress lists (1986-1993). Meenakshi is known for her proficiency in both acting and dancing.[[26]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-26)

Often referred to as _"Damini,"_ she is famous for her dance in the song "Tu Mera Hero Hai" from the film _Hero_. She is also known for her dance sequences to Bollywood songs, such as "Pyar Karne Wale" (from _Hero_), "Rock' N' Roll," "Tu Nache Main Gaoon" with Mithun (from _Main Balwaan_ and _Parivaar_), "Teri Payal Mere Geet" with Govinda (from _Teri Payal Mere Geet_), "Jaane Do Jaane Do" (from _Shahenshah_) opposite Amitabh Bachchan, "Badal Pe Chalke" (from _Vijay_) opposite Anil Kapoor and Rishi Kapoor, "Bin Saajan Jhula" (from _Damini_) opposite [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan"), "Sajan Mera Uss Par Hai" (from _[Gangaa Jamunaa Saraswati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangaa\_Jamunaa\_Saraswati "Gangaa Jamunaa Saraswati")_), "Mujre Wali Hoon" (from _[Awaargi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awaargi "Awaargi")_), "Jab Koi Baat Bigad Jaye" (from _Jurm_), and "Badan Main Chandni" (from [_Ghatak_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghatak:_Lethal "Ghatak: Lethal")).

She considers herself more of a dancer than an actress.[[7]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-rmrmedia1-7) Her desire to continue the art and extend this culture in a foreign land led her to found the Cherish Dance School.[[7]](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Seshadri&h=AUBJlfryqpC0Vp4sEWp_Jdf5TRvXd0dbz_JqNkJVd2HEkYJSkK5OEHyHny8araUM2lOZKdYKlFY_JYzG-gHFhYkBkaJaMDa237bUhlJKFdZWX2ocJCCzvmZdiYRQ99TNZ2AWW1DUThJ0ZA#cite_note-rmrmedia1-7)

### Singing

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Singing")]

Meenakshi sang some poetic notes in J.P. Dutta's movie _Kshatriya_, in a composition by Laxmikant Pyarelal. She sang a song in another movie, _Tadap_, with [Chunky Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chunky_Pandey "Chunky Pandey") and [Nana Patekar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Patekar "Nana Patekar"), but the movie was not released. She sang "Tumhare Roop Ka", composed by [R.D. Burman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._D._Burman "R. D. Burman"), with [Amit Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amit_Kumar "Amit Kumar") and [Suresh Wadkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suresh_Wadkar "Suresh Wadkar").

## Documentaries and television appearances

[[edit](https://l.facebook.com/w/index.php?title=Meenakshi_Seshadri&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Documentaries and television appearances")]

She has made few appearances on talk shows and rarely gives interviews.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In 1987, she appeared in an interview in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), in which she discussed her personal and professional life.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1992, Meenakshi featured in the television documentary _World of Film: India_ about the Indian film industry; she appeared with stalwarts such as [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor"), Amitabh Bachchan, and [Mira Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mira_Nair "Mira Nair").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1997, she made a rare public appearance on [Shekhar Suman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Suman "Shekhar Suman")'s talk show _[Movers & Shakers (TV series)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movers\_&\_Shakers\_(TV\_series) "Movers & Shakers (TV series)")_; this was also her last television appearance before she left the industry to raise her children.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] She discussed her entire career, her personal life, and her passion for dance and her stage performances.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2006, a documentary was made on her life called _Meenakshi Accept Her Wings_, directed by Margret Stephens; the two-hour musical documentary depicted her lifestyle transition from a dancer and actress to a homemaker.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The movie gave a deeper insight to her life after quitting film and her successful marriage.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

**Twinkle Khanna** (born 29 December 1973)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-2) is an Indian author, columnist and former actress. She has published the non-fiction collection Mrs Funnybones (2015), the short story collection The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad (2016), the novel Pyjamas Are Forgiving (2018), the short story collection Welcome to Paradise (2023) and Mrs Funnybones Returns (2025), a sequel to her first book.

The daughter of actors [Dimple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimple_Kapadia "Dimple Kapadia") and [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna"), she made her acting debut in a leading role in Barsaat (1995), for which she received the [Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Female_Debut "Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut"). After appearing as the leading lady in films including [Jaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaan_(film) "Jaan (film)") (1996), [Jab Pyaar Kisise Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jab_Pyaar_Kisise_Hota_Hai "Jab Pyaar Kisise Hota Hai") (1998), [International Khiladi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Khiladi "International Khiladi") (1999), [Baadshah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baadshah_(1999_film) "Baadshah (1999 film)") (1999) and [Love Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Ke_Liye_Kuch_Bhi_Karega "Love Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega") (2001), she left the film industry.

Khanna subsequently worked as an interior designer and began writing newspaper opinion columns, later collected in her first book. In 2019 she founded Tweak India, a bilingual digital media platform aimed at women. She holds a master's degree in fiction writing from Goldsmiths, University of London.

In 2025 she co-hosted the [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_video "Prime video") talk show Two Much with [Kajol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kajol "Kajol") and Twinkle alongside the actress Kajol. Prime Video reported it as its most-watched unscripted Indian original series.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-5)

Khanna is married to the actor [Akshay Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akshay_Kumar "Akshay Kumar"), with whom she has two children.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Twinkle_Khanna&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Twinkle Khanna was born on 29 December 1973 in [Bombay, Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay,_Maharashtra "Bombay, Maharashtra"), the first of two daughters of veteran [Hindi film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_film "Hindi film") actors, [Dimple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimple_Kapadia "Dimple Kapadia") and [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna"), with whom she shared her birthday.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-HT-6) Her maternal grandfather, Chunnibhai Kapadia was a businessman. Her mother is a [Gujarati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarati_people "Gujarati people") and her father, Rajesh Khanna, a [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_people "Punjabi people") from [Amritsar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amritsar "Amritsar"), was from a family of railway contractors.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-9) On her mother's side, she is the niece of the actress and costume designer [Simple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_Kapadia "Simple Kapadia")..[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-10) Khanna has said that she did not experience patriarchy while growing up alongside her sister, [Rinke Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinke_Khanna "Rinke Khanna"), who, like their cousin [Karan Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Kapadia "Karan Kapadia"), has also acted in films.

.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-13)

Khanna attended the [New Era High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Era_High_School "New Era High School") in [Panchgani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panchgani "Panchgani") and the [Narsee Monjee College of Commerce and Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narsee_Monjee_College_of_Commerce_and_Economics "Narsee Monjee College of Commerce and Economics") of the [University of Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Mumbai "University of Mumbai") in [Vile Parle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vile_Parle "Vile Parle").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-14)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-HT-6)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Rediff-15) After finishing her [Class 12th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_examination "Board examination"), she wanted to pursue a career as a [chartered accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chartered_accountant "Chartered accountant") and took the entrance examination, but joined the film industry instead due to the insistence of her parents.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Rediff-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-16)

She later pursued a [Master of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts "Master of Arts") from [Goldsmiths, University of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldsmiths,_University_of_London "Goldsmiths, University of London") in the [New Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Cross "New Cross") area of [Lewisham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Borough_of_Lewisham "London Borough of Lewisham"), graduating in 2024.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-17)

## Acting career (1995–2001)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Twinkle_Khanna&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Acting career (1995–2001)")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Twinkle_Khanna_still4.jpg/250px-Twinkle_Khanna_still4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Twinkle_Khanna_still4.jpg)

Khanna in 2010

Khanna made her screen debut opposite [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol") in [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi")'s musical romance _[Barsaat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barsaat\_(1995\_film) "Barsaat (1995 film)")_ (1995). She was cast by [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra") and before the film's release Khanna signed for two more projects.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-18) It performed well at the box office and became the sixth-highest-grossing film of the year,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-19) and she received the [Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Female_Debut "Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut") for her performance.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Debut-20) The following year she played lead roles in [Raj Kanwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kanwar "Raj Kanwar")'s action film _[Jaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaan\_(film) "Jaan (film)")_ and [Lawrence D'Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_D'Souza "Lawrence D'Souza")'s romance _[Dil Tera Diwana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Tera\_Diwana\_(1996\_film) "Dil Tera Diwana (1996 film)")_ opposite [Ajay Devgn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajay_Devgn "Ajay Devgn") and [Saif Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan") respectively. _Jaan was a box office hit and Dil Tera Diwana did not perform well._[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-21) K.N. Vijiyan of the _[New Straits Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Straits\_Times "New Straits Times")_ wrote that "Khanna does not look like a typical Hindi actress".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-22) While reviewing _[Dil Tera Diwana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Tera\_Diwana\_(1996\_film) "Dil Tera Diwana (1996 film)")_, Vijiyan wrote about Khanna: "Unlike her previous movies, she looks really good in all her scenes and she can act well."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-23)

In 1997, two films featuring her; _[Uff! Yeh Mohabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uff!\_Yeh\_Mohabbat "Uff! Yeh Mohabbat")_ and _[Itihaas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itihaas\_(1997\_film) "Itihaas (1997 film)")_ were released. Both of these films were poor box office performers.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-25) Her only release in 1998 was _[Jab Pyaar Kisise Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jab\_Pyaar\_Kisise\_Hota\_Hai "Jab Pyaar Kisise Hota Hai")_, which featured her as [Salman Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan")'s love interest and was a box office success.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-27) Khanna acted opposite Akshay Kumar in two action films: _[International Khiladi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International\_Khiladi "International Khiladi")_ and _[Zulmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zulmi "Zulmi")_ (both 1999). In the former she played a news reporter who falls in love with a criminal whom she interviews. Both performed poorly at the box office.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-28) She was paired with [Daggubati Venkatesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daggubati_Venkatesh "Daggubati Venkatesh") in the [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") film _[Seenu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seenu\_(1999\_film) "Seenu (1999 film)")_ (1999).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-29)

Khanna played the lead role in _[Baadshah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baadshah\_(1999\_film) "Baadshah (1999 film)")_ (1999), featuring [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") as a detective.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Sen2012-30) In the same year, she acted opposite Saif Ali Khan in _[Yeh Hai Mumbai Meri Jaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeh\_Hai\_Mumbai\_Meri\_Jaan "Yeh Hai Mumbai Meri Jaan")_, a romantic comedy directed by [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt"). She was paired opposite [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") in [Dharmesh Darshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmesh_Darshan "Dharmesh Darshan")'s _[Mela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mela\_(2000\_film) "Mela (2000 film)")_ (2000). Similar to _The Seven Samurai_ in story,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Mela-31) it was an average grosser at the box office.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-32)_[Chal Mere Bhai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chal\_Mere\_Bhai "Chal Mere Bhai")_ (2000) featured Khanna in a special appearance beside a leading role in the comedy _[Joru Ka Ghulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joru\_Ka\_Ghulam\_(2000\_film) "Joru Ka Ghulam (2000 film)")_, opposite [Govinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Govinda_(actor) "Govinda (actor)"). She also acted in the [David Dhawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dhawan "David Dhawan")-directed comedy _[Jodi No.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodi\_No.1\_(film) "Jodi No.1 (film)")_ (2001).[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Zaidi2014-33) Her acting in the film met with poor reviews.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-34)

Film director [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar") admitted in an interview that Khanna was in his mind for the role of Tina in _[Kuch Kuch Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuch\_Kuch\_Hota\_Hai "Kuch Kuch Hota Hai")_,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Debut-20) but she refused it, and thus [Rani Mukerji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rani_Mukerji "Rani Mukerji") was signed.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-35) She left the industry after her marriage to Akshay Kumar in 2001, citing that she did not enjoy the acting profession any more.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-36) Her last film was _[Love Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Ke\_Liye\_Kuch\_Bhi\_Karega "Love Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega")_ (2001), a remake of the Telugu movie _[Money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money\_(1993\_film) "Money (1993 film)")_ (1993).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-37) It featured her opposite [Fardeen Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fardeen_Khan "Fardeen Khan") and was an average grosser at the box office.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Box_office-38)

## Off-screen work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Twinkle_Khanna&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Off-screen work")]

In August and October 1999, Khanna performed in the Awesome Foursome concert held at the Shah Alam Outdoor Stadium, [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia") and the Magnificent Five concert at [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), England. [Juhi Chawla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla"), [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") and [Salman Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan") accompanied her in the former while in the latter she performed alongside [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan"), [Aishwarya Rai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aishwarya_Rai "Aishwarya Rai"), [Akshaye Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akshaye_Khanna "Akshaye Khanna") and [Rani Mukerji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rani_Mukherjee "Rani Mukherjee").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-41) The following year, she was part of the judge panel at [Femina Miss India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femina_Miss_India "Femina Miss India").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Pathak2006-42) She made her theatre debut as the female lead in Feroz Khan's _All The Best_ in February 2001.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-43) In 2002, Khanna opened her own interior design store in [Crawford Market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crawford_Market "Crawford Market"), [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"), called The White Window, in partnership with her longtime friend Gurlein Manchanda. Since then, the store has received the Elle Decor International Design Award.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Galaxy-44) She has opened up another branch of the store elsewhere in Mumbai.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-TKLKF-45) She does not hold a professional degree and worked with an architect for two years to learn the procedures.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Galaxy-44) During her pregnancy, she practised maps and designs using [CAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-aided_design "Computer-aided design").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-46) Khanna did the interiors for [Rani Mukerji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rani_Mukerji "Rani Mukerji")'s,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-47)[Reemma Sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reemma_Sen "Reemma Sen")'s[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-48) and [Tabu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabu_(actress) "Tabu (actress)")'s houses,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-49)[Kareena Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kareena_Kapoor "Kareena Kapoor")'s Bandra flat in 2008[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-50) and Poonam Bajaj's design studio.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-51) On the request of one of her clients, she ordered a company to make a golden toilet seat.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-52) In 2017, Khanna was signed as the Indian [brand ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_ambassador "Brand ambassador") for [L'Oréal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Or%C3%A9al "L'Oréal") Professionnel.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-53)

Khanna attends Save The Children event

Khanna has also endorsed for and designed Supertech's ORB project in Noida and another residential project in Pune.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-55) However, Khanna filed a case against Supertech for failing to pay ₹10.4 million (US$110,000) as endorsement fees.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-56) She also mentors International Institute of Fashion Designing's Academy of Interiors.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-57) Khanna is the co-founder of [Grazing Goat Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grazing_Goat_Pictures "Grazing Goat Pictures") and has co-produced the films _[Tees Maar Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tees\_Maar\_Khan\_(2010\_film) "Tees Maar Khan (2010 film)")_ (2010) and _[Patiala House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patiala\_House\_(film) "Patiala House (film)")_ (2011).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-58) She also did a cameo appearance in the former film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-TMK-59) Khanna has also co-produced _[Thank You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_(2011\_film) "Thank You (2011 film)")_ (2011), _[Khiladi 786](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khiladi\_786 "Khiladi 786")_ (2012), and _[72 Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/72\_Miles "72 Miles")_ (2013). She has also been the brand ambassador for the watch brand [Movado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movado "Movado") and endorsed [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola") and [Micromax Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micromax_Mobile "Micromax Mobile").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-MAJUMDAR2007-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-62) In December 2016, Khanna launched her production house, Mrs. Funnybones Movies, which eventually co-produced _Pad Man_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-64) The film went on to win the 2018 [National Film Award for Best Film on Other Social Issues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Film_on_Other_Social_Issues "National Film Award for Best Film on Other Social Issues").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-65)

Khanna has written weekly opinion columns for DNA After Hours, the weekend supplement of [Daily News and Analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_News_and_Analysis "Daily News and Analysis"), and for [The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times_of_India "The Times of India"). The columns, written under the byline Mrs Funnybones, formed the basis of her first book.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-66) In 2015, [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House") announced that [Mrs Funnybones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs_Funnybones "Mrs Funnybones") had entered the Nielsen bestseller list at number two in its first week of sales. Launched in Mumbai on 18 August 2015, the book reached number one on the bestseller chart of Crossword's Kemps Corner store. According to Nielsen BookScan India, it made Khanna the highest-selling female author in India that year.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-69) Khanna's second book _[The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Lakshmi\_Prasad "The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad")_, a collection of four short stories, launched in November 2016 sold more than 100,000 copies.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-71) Her third book, the novel [Pyjamas Are Forgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyjamas_Are_Forgiving "Pyjamas Are Forgiving"), was published by Juggernaut Books in September 2018. According to Nielsen BookScan India it debuted at number one on the all-India bestseller list, and the publisher reported sales of more than 100,000 copies.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-74)

Khanna has been active in advocating the cause of [menstrual hygiene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminine_hygiene "Feminine hygiene"). She joined hands with Save the Children to promote the right to menstrual hygiene among children and slum communities.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-75) She was invited to speak at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") in 2018.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-76) She was also invited to be a part of an eminent panel at the United Nations, New York and also appeared on BBC world Impact show to talk about menstrual hygiene and sanitation globally.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-78)

In 2019, Khanna founded Tweak India, a bilingual digital media platform for women covering subjects including parenting, body image, mental health, [LGBTQI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQI "LGBTQI") issues, wellness and sustainability.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-81)

In 2022, Khanna went onto pursue her master's in fiction writing at [Goldsmiths, University of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldsmiths,_University_of_London "Goldsmiths, University of London").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-83) She received a distinction for her final dissertation, and was one of the shortlistees for the Pat Kavanagh Prize.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-85)

## Personal life

In 2001, Khanna campaigned for her father's election in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "New Delhi (Lok Sabha constituency)").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-Roy1996-86) She met [Akshay Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akshay_Kumar "Akshay Kumar"), for the first time during a photo session for _[Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")_ magazine.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-87) They got married on 17 January 2001 and together have a son, Aarav and a daughter, Nitara.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-89) Kumar often credits Khanna for his success.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-91) In 2009, _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_ magazine listed her as the fourth-best-dressed celebrity in India.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-92)

In 2014, Khanna and her sister sold their father's house for 85 [crores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crore "Crore").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-93) She has maintained a [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") account since November 2014.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle_Khanna#cite_note-94)

Amitabh Bachchan[a] (né Srivastava;[1] born 11 October 1942) is an Indian actor, playback singer, and producer who primarily works in Hindi cinema. Widely considered one of the greatest, most accomplished and commercially successful actors in the history of Indian cinema,[7] he has starred in over 200 films. Bachchan has been called "the Angry Young Man", the Shahenshah of Bollywood, Sadi ke Mahanayak (literally meaning "superstar of the century"), Bollywood's Star of the Millennium, or simply Big B.[8] His dominance in the Indian film industry during the 1970s–80s led the French director François Truffaut to describe him as a "one-man industry".[9] He is a recipient of several accolades including seven National Film Awards and seventeen Filmfare Awards & one South Filmfare award.

Bachchan was born in Allahabad (now Prayagraj), and he was educated at Sherwood College, Nainital, Uttarakhand and Kirori Mal College, University of Delhi. His film career started in 1969 as a voice narrator in Mrinal Sen's film Bhuvan Shome and first gained popularity in the early-1970s, with films, such as Anand, Zanjeer, Namak Haraam and Roti Kapda Aur Makaan.[10][11] He achieved greater stardom in later years, being dubbed as "Angry Young Man" for several of his on-screen roles in Hindi films. He consistently starred in a number of top-grossing Hindi films from the mid-1970s to the 1980s, such as Deewaar, Sholay, Kabhi Kabhie, Hera Pheri, Amar Akbar Anthony, Parvarish, Trishul, Don, Muqaddar Ka Sikandar, Kasme Vaade, Suhaag, Kaala Patthar, Dostana, Naseeb, Lawaaris, Namak Halaal, Khud-Daar, Coolie, Andhaa Kanoon, Sharaabi and Mard.[12] Some of his most acclaimed performances, include Majboor, Chupke Chupke, Mili, Do Anjaane, Alaap, The Great Gambler, Shaan, Barsaat Ki Ek Raat, Silsila, Kaalia, Satte Pe Satta, Bemisal, Shakti, Aakhree Raasta and Shahenshah.[13] Bachchan was voted the "greatest star of stage or screen" in the BBC Your Millennium online users poll in 1999.[14] In October 2003, Time magazine said he is the undisputed godfather of Bollywood.[15]

After taking a break from acting in the 1990s, Bachchan's resurgence was marked in 2000 with Mohabbatein.[16] Since then he starred in several successful and acclaimed films like Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, Aankhen, Baghban, Veer-Zaara, Khakee, Black, Sarkar, Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna, Cheeni Kum, Paa, Piku, Pink, Badla, Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva and Kalki 2898 AD.[17] He also made an appearance in the Hollywood film, The Great Gatsby (2013), in which he played a non-Indian Jewish character.[18]

Bachchan has won numerous accolades in his career, including record four National Film Awards in Best Actor category and many awards at international film festivals and award ceremonies. He has won sixteen Filmfare Awards and is the most nominated performer in any major acting category at Filmfare with 34 nominations in Best Actor and 42 nominations overall. The Government of India honoured him with the Padma Shri in 1984, the Padma Bhushan in 2001, the Padma Vibhushan in 2015, and India's highest award in the field of cinema, the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2018 for his contributions to the arts. The Government of France honoured him with its highest civilian honour, Officer of the Legion of Honour, in 2007 for his exceptional career in the world of cinema and beyond.

In addition to acting, Bachchan has worked as a playback singer, film producer, and television presenter. He has hosted several seasons of the game show Kaun Banega Crorepati, which is the Indian version of the game show franchise, Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?. He also entered politics for a time in the 1980s. Bachchan has also been involved in several humanitarian works and he is a brand endorser in India. Beyond the Indian subcontinent, he acquired a large overseas following of the South Asian diaspora, as well as others, in markets including Africa (South Africa, Eastern Africa, and Mauritius), the Middle East (especially Egypt and the UAE), the United Kingdom, Russia, Central Asia, the Caribbean (Guyana, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago), Oceania (Fiji, Australia, and New Zealand), Canada and the United States.[19]

Early life and family
Further information: Bachchan family

Bachchan was born on 11 October 1942[20] in Allahabad (now Prayagraj) to Hindi poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan and social activist Teji Bachchan.[21] Harivansh Rai Bachchan was an Awadhi Hindu Kayastha,[22] who was fluent in Awadhi,[23] Hindi and Urdu.[24] Harivansh's ancestors came from a village called Babupatti, in the Raniganj tehsil, in the Pratapgarh district, in the present-day state of Uttar Pradesh, in India.[25] Teji Bachchan was a Punjabi Sikh Khatri from Lyallpur, Punjab, British India (present-day Faisalabad, Punjab, Pakistan).[23][26] Bachchan has a younger brother, Ajitabh, who is five years younger than him.[27]

Bachchan's parents were initially going to name him Inquilaab (Hindustani for "Revolution"), inspired by the phrase Inquilab Zindabad ("Long live the revolution") popularly used during the Indian independence struggle; the name Amitabh was suggested to his father by poet Sumitranandan Pant.[28][1] Although his surname was Srivastava, Amitabh's father, who opposed the caste system, had adopted the pen name Bachchan ("child-like" in colloquial Hindi), under which he published all of his works.[29] When his father was looking to get him admitted to a school, he and Bachchan's mother decided the family's name should be Bachchan instead of Shrivastava.[30] It is with this last name that Amitabh debuted in films and used for all other practical purposes, Bachchan has become the surname for all of his immediate family.[31] Bachchan's father died in 2003, and his mother in 2007.[32]

Bachchan's secondary education was at Boys' High School & College in Allahabad and Sherwood College in Nainital. He attended Kirori Mal College at the University of Delhi in Delhi.[33][34] He graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree from Kirori Mal College in 1962.[35][36][37] When Bachchan finished his studies, his father approached Prithviraj Kapoor, the founder of Prithvi Theatre and patriarch of the Kapoor acting family, to see if there was an opening for him, but Kapoor offered no encouragement.[38] Bachchan was a friend of Rajiv Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi, before he became an actor. He used to spend time with them when he was a resident in New Delhi. Bachchan's family were very close to the Nehru-Gandhi family of politicians. When Sonia Gandhi first came to India from Italy before her marriage, Bachchan had received her at the Palam International Airport on 13 January 1968. She spent 48 days at Bachchan's house with his parents before her wedding to Rajiv.[39]

In the late 1960s, Bachchan applied to be a newsreader for All India Radio in Delhi, but "failed the audition".[38][40] He became a business executive for Bird & Company in Kolkata (Calcutta),[38] [when?] and worked in theatre before starting his film career.[41] It is thought that his mother might have had some influence on his choice of career, for she always insisted that he should "take centre stage".[42][according to whom?]

Acting career
Further information: Amitabh Bachchan filmography
Early career (1969–1972)

Bachchan made his film debut in 1969, as a voice narrator in Mrinal Sen's National Award–winning film Bhuvan Shome.[43] His first acting role was as one of the seven protagonists in the film Saat Hindustani,[44] directed by Khwaja Ahmad Abbas and featuring Utpal Dutt, Anwar Ali (brother of comedian Mehmood), Madhu and Jalal Agha.[45][46] Anand (1971) followed, in which Bachchan starred alongside Rajesh Khanna. His role as a doctor with a cynical view of life garnered Bachchan his first Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor. He then played his first antagonist role as an infatuated lover-turned-murderer in Parwana (1971). Following Parwana, he starred in several films, including Sunil Dutt's Reshma Aur Shera (1971) where he played a mute character. During this time, he made a guest appearance in the film Guddi which starred his future wife Jaya Bhaduri. He narrated part of the film Bawarchi.[47] In 1972, he made an appearance in the road action comedy Bombay to Goa directed by S. Ramanathan which was moderately successful.[48] Many of Bachchan's films during this early period did not do well.[49] His only film with Mala Sinha, Sanjog (1972) was also a box office failure.[50]

Rise to prominence (1973–1974)

Bachchan was struggling, seen as a "failed newcomer" who, by the age of 30, had only two successes (as a lead in Bombay to Goa and a supporting role in Anand).[51] Bachchan was then discovered by screenwriter duo Salim–Javed, consisting of Salim Khan and Javed Akhtar.[52] Salim Khan wrote the story, screenplay and script of Zanjeer (1973), and conceived the "angry young man" persona of the lead role. Javed Akhtar came on board as co-writer,[53] and Prakash Mehra, who saw the script as potentially groundbreaking, as the film's director. However, they were struggling to find an actor for the lead "angry young man" role; it was turned down by several actors, owing to it going against the "romantic hero" image dominant in the industry at the time.[52] Salim-Javed "saw his talent, which most makers didn't. He was exceptional, a genius actor who was in films that weren't good."[54] According to Salim Khan, they "strongly felt that Amitabh was the ideal casting for Zanjeer".[52] Salim Khan introduced Bachchan to Prakash Mehra,[53] and Salim-Javed insisted that Bachchan be cast for the role.[52]

Zanjeer was a crime film with violent action,[52] in sharp contrast to the romantically themed films that had generally preceded it, and it established Amitabh in a new persona—the "angry young man" of Bollywood.[55] He earned his first Filmfare Award nomination for Best Actor, with Filmfare later considering this one of the most iconic performances in Bollywood history.[49] The film was a blockbuster and one of the highest-grossing films of that year, breaking Bachchan's dry spell at the box office and making him a star.[56][57] It was the first of many collaborations between Salim-Javed and Amitabh; the duo wrote many of their subsequent scripts with Bachchan in mind for the lead role, and insisted on him being cast for their later films.[54] Salim Khan also introduced Bachchan to director Manmohan Desai with whom he formed a long and successful association, alongside Prakash Mehra and Yash Chopra.[53]

Eventually, Bachchan became one of the most successful leading men of the film industry. His portrayal of the wronged hero fighting a crooked system and circumstances of deprivation in films like Zanjeer, Deewaar, Trishul, Kaala Patthar and Shakti resonated with the masses of the time, especially the youth who harboured a simmering discontent owing to social ills such as poverty, hunger, unemployment, corruption, social inequality and the brutal excesses of The Emergency. This led to Bachchan being dubbed as the "angry young man", a journalistic catchphrase that became a metaphor for the dormant rage, frustration, restlessness, sense of rebellion and anti-establishment disposition of an entire generation, prevalent in the 1970s.[58][59][60]

The year 1973 was also when he married Jaya, and around this time they appeared in several films together: not only Zanjeer but also subsequent films such as Abhimaan, which was released around the same time after their wedding and was also successful at the box office.[61] Later, he played the role of Vikram, once again along with Rajesh Khanna, in the film Namak Haraam, a social drama directed by Hrishikesh Mukherjee and addressing themes of friendship.[62] The film proved to be a superhit and Bachchan won his second Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor for his performance.[62][63] The flow of successes continued for Bachchan in 1974.[64] He began the year with a guest appearance in Dulal Guha's blockbuster social drama film Dost.[65] After this, he starred in Aravind Sen's drama film Kasauti and Narendra Bedi's crime thriller Benaam, both of which ended up as moderate commercial successes. Bachchan's next release was Manoj Kumar's fourth directional venture Roti Kapada Aur Makaan.[66] The film opened to excellent response all over the country, eventually taking top spot at the box office that year and emerging an All Time Blockbuster as well as Bachchan's biggest hit up to that point of time.[67] Before the end of year, he delivered a hit in Ravi Tandon's crime thriller Majboor.[68] Written by Salim-Javed, it also had Pran and Parveen Babi in the lead.[69]

Peak years (1975–1988)

In 1975, Bachchan starred in a variety of film genres, from the comedy Chupke Chupke and the crime drama Faraar to the romantic drama Mili.[70] This was also the year in which he starred in two films regarded as important in Hindi cinema history, both written by Salim-Javed, who again insisted on casting Bachchan.[54] The first was Deewaar, directed by Yash Chopra, where he worked with Shashi Kapoor, Nirupa Roy, Parveen Babi, and Neetu Singh. The film emerged a blockbuster at the box office and earned him another Filmfare nomination for Best Actor.[71] Indiatimes ranks Deewaar among the Top 25 Must See Bollywood Films.[72] The other, released on 15 August 1975, was Sholay, which became the highest-grossing film ever in India at the time,[73] in which Bachchan played the role of Jaidev. Deewaar and Sholay are often credited with exalting Bachchan to the heights of superstardom, two years after he became a star with Zanjeer, and consolidating his domination of the industry throughout the 1970s and 1980s.[74][75] In 1999, BBC India declared Sholay the "Film of the Millennium" and, like Deewaar, it has been cited by Indiatimes Movies as among the Top 25 Must See Bollywood Films.[72] In that same year, the judges of the 50th annual Filmfare Awards awarded it with the special distinction award called the Filmfare Best Film of 50 Years.

Bachchan and Dharmendra starrer Sholay (1975) recorded an estimated ₹15-18 crore footfalls, making it the highest grossing Indian film in terms of audience attendance to date.[76]

In 1976, he was cast by Yash Chopra in the romantic musical Kabhi Kabhie.[77] Bachchan starred as a young poet, Amit Malhotra, who falls deeply in love with a beautiful young girl named Pooja (Rakhee Gulzar) who ends up marrying someone else (Shashi Kapoor). The film was notable for portraying Bachchan as a romantic hero, a far cry from his "angry young man" roles like Zanjeer and Deewaar. Despite its heavy theme, Kabhi Kabhie went on to become a superhit.[78] Its soundtrack composed by Khayyam and lyrics written by Sahir Ludhianvi dominated the year-end annual list of Binaca Geetmala and was one of the best-selling Hindi film albums of the 1970s.[79] Bachchan was again nominated for the Filmfare Best Actor Award for his role in the film. That same year, he played a double role in another hit Adalat as father and son. In 1977, he won his first Filmfare Best Actor Award for his performance in Amar Akbar Anthony, in which he played the third lead opposite Vinod Khanna and Rishi Kapoor as Anthony Gonsalves. The film was the highest-grossing film of that year. His other major hits that year include Parvarish and Khoon Pasina.[80]

He once again resumed double roles in films such as Kasme Vaade (1978) as Amit and Shankar and Don (1978) playing the characters of Don, a leader of an underworld gang and his look-alike Vijay. His performance won him his second Filmfare Best Actor Award. He also gave towering performances in Yash Chopra's Trishul and Prakash Mehra's Muqaddar Ka Sikandar both of which earned him further Filmfare Best Actor nominations. 1978 is arguably considered his most successful year at the box office since all of his six releases in the same year, namely Muqaddar Ka Sikandar, Trishul, Don, Kasme Vaade, Ganga Ki Saugandh and Besharam were box office successes, with the former three being the consecutive highest-grossing films of the year, a rare feat in Hindi cinema.[81][82]

In 1979, Bachchan starred in Suhaag which was the highest-earning film of that year.[67] In the same year, he also enjoyed critical acclaim and commercial success with films like Jurmana, Mr. Natwarlal and Kaala Patthar.[83] He was required to use his singing voice for the first time in a song from the film Mr. Natwarlal in which he starred with Rekha. Bachchan's performance in the film saw him nominated for both the Filmfare Award for Best Actor and the Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer. Her breakthrough in Hindi cinema came with the 1971 film "Guddi," directed by Hrishikesh Mukherjee, where she played the titular role of a schoolgirl obsessed with film star Dharmendra. "Guddi" established her "girl-next-door" image, which became a hallmark of her early career and contributed to her rapid rise as a popular actress in Bollywood.

[September 22 at 9:55 PM](https://www.facebook.com/OldenIndianCinema/posts/pfbid025JdLoj9NMXukpwT7GySbRbGXdRuNY7AEQiDKTc6TULXuevHtgn7fFBQeNwZcQ4TRl?__cft__[0 [link_2]]=AZjtviIpeMam2W4Zo1swHwhV0TTT3Hnc3CHoG-iXDBszQWZde2MHrNnOag6YKJQ1liswoLYN3IrWTRfVbEyF38AOPW6sxFf1HnkzvcXK_5NvIXF9G8EBCE2JgupUaY72ML5ZABgbn1WjJ_SyEMVMyq2JIv79Z3hK&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R) · 

Tanuja and Jaya Bachchan belong to a generation of actresses whose careers began when Hindi cinema was changing rapidly in the 1960s. Tanuja found memorable roles in films such as Jewel Thief, Haathi Mere Saathi, Anubhav and Mere Jeevan Saathi, while Jaya became known for films including Guddi, Koshish, Abhimaan, Mili, Chupke Chupke and Sholay. 

Tanishaa Mukerji, Tanuja’s daughter, shared this photograph in October 2025 with the simple caption, “What an epic pic! [#Throwback](https://www.facebook.com/hashtag/throwback?__eep__=6&__cft__[0 [link_3]]=AZjtviIpeMam2W4Zo1swHwhV0TTT3Hnc3CHoG-iXDBszQWZde2MHrNnOag6YKJQ1liswoLYN3IrWTRfVbEyF38AOPW6sxFf1HnkzvcXK_5NvIXF9G8EBCE2JgupUaY72ML5ZABgbn1WjJ_SyEMVMyq2JIv79Z3hK&__tn__=*NK-R)[#Tanuja](https://www.facebook.com/hashtag/tanuja?__eep__=6&__cft__[0 [link_4]]=AZjtviIpeMam2W4Zo1swHwhV0TTT3Hnc3CHoG-iXDBszQWZde2MHrNnOag6YKJQ1liswoLYN3IrWTRfVbEyF38AOPW6sxFf1HnkzvcXK_5NvIXF9G8EBCE2JgupUaY72ML5ZABgbn1WjJ_SyEMVMyq2JIv79Z3hK&__tn__=*NK-R)[#JayaBachchan](https://www.facebook.com/hashtag/jayabachchan?__eep__=6&__cft__[0 [link_5]]=AZjtviIpeMam2W4Zo1swHwhV0TTT3Hnc3CHoG-iXDBszQWZde2MHrNnOag6YKJQ1liswoLYN3IrWTRfVbEyF38AOPW6sxFf1HnkzvcXK_5NvIXF9G8EBCE2JgupUaY72ML5ZABgbn1WjJ_SyEMVMyq2JIv79Z3hK&__tn__=*NK-R).” The picture was taken at a festive gathering, bringing together two actresses who had been part of Hindi cinema for decades. 

There is also a family connection behind the photograph. Tanuja is the mother of Kajol and Tanishaa, while Jaya is the mother of Abhishek Bachchan and Shweta Bachchan Nanda. Tanishaa has continued to share photographs that connect her family with people from her mother’s generation of cinema.

Jaya Bhaduri, now Jaya Bachchan, made her acting debut at the age of 15 in the acclaimed Bengali film "Mahanagar" (1963), directed by Satyajit Ray. Her breakthrough in Hindi cinema came with the 1971 film "Guddi," directed by Hrishikesh Mukherjee, where she played the titular role of a schoolgirl obsessed with film star Dharmendra. "Guddi" established her "girl-next-door" image, which became a hallmark of her early career and contributed to her rapid rise as a popular actress in Bollywood.
